# Remedy

> Remedy turns proof of destruction into a payment trigger. When a recall says "destroy it and send a photo," the owner logs in with PayPal, writes a one-time code on the recalled unit and cuts it apart in front of a live camera. Code checks the evidence, and the refund lands in the exact PayPal account that logged in: on claim RM-0442 it was sent to PayPal 15 seconds after the photo, and PayPal confirmed it at 55 seconds. No account, no form, no email. Settlement tools verify the person. Remedy verifies the product is destroyed.

## The problem

- Only 6–10% of recalled products are ever returned or destroyed ([PIRG, 2024](https://publicinterestnetwork.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/TOO-MUCH-TO-RECALL-FINAL-1-11-1.pdf)).
- Refunds still run on email: in our count of the [CPSC recalls API](https://www.saferproducts.gov/RestWebServices/Recall?format=json&RecallDateStart=2026-10-01&RecallDateEnd=2026-11-05), 1 Oct to 5 Nov 2026, 20 of the 27 refund recalls that required a photo told owners to email it, some to @gmail.com inboxes.
- The CPSC names "artificially generated images… purporting to demonstrate product destruction" as a threat, and warns that fraud controls can "reduce recall participation" ([RFI CPSC-2026-0067](https://public-inspection.federalregister.gov/2026-07328.pdf)). Remedy answers both: easy for honest owners, no payout for a photo that isn't tied to a live claim.

## Try it now

- [Claim a refund](https://remedy-recalls.vercel.app/r/kikea-x-vesolje/try): Phone-first, on real recall CPSC 27-071 (X-VESOLJE nursing pillows, about 19,596 units, suffocation risk, $29.99 refund). Demo PayPal account on the page.
- [Company console](https://remedy-recalls.vercel.app/signin): The evidence room a recalling company works from. Demo account on the page.
- [Home](https://remedy-recalls.vercel.app/): The whole story in one scroll.

## Why a fake can't get paid

Remedy doesn't bet on spotting AI images. It makes a fake worthless, and the first three checks use no AI:

1. **Sent in the camera session.** No upload button: laptop webcam, or a phone through a QR hand-off. Photos must arrive inside the claim's 10-minute camera session, carrying its key.
2. **Photo not used before.** A perceptual fingerprint compares every photo against every earlier claim.
3. **One verified PayPal account, one claim per recall.** Whoever proves the destruction is paid, in their own verified name.
4. **A code that didn't exist ten minutes ago.** Letter, digit, letter, no look-alike characters, read back character by character. No web, stock or old photo can carry it. CPSC recalls already have owners write on the unit (HotHands, 27-011).
5. **Really destroyed, really the recalled product.** GPT-6.1 Sol reads the label and each step of the cut, quoting what it sees, in schema-validated output.

**Code decides, never the model.** Any "no" rejects, any "unclear" goes to a person, and only a pass on every check pays.

## Results

- **Sent to PayPal 15 seconds after the photo, confirmed by PayPal at 55 seconds** (claim RM-0442). A passing claim is usually paid within a minute.
- **Zero web photos ever paid** with the code check on. Every wrong code caught.
- **Genuine owners paid**, including on claims the system had never seen, where 96% of the model's check answers were right. Every answer carries a quote a reviewer can check.
- **$0.011 of AI per claim**, about 16 seconds of vision. A penny to verify a refund.
- **Passes all four of PIRG's easy-refund tests:** online, one sitting, photo proof, real money.

## PayPal is the product

- **Log in with PayPal (OpenID Connect):** The verified payer ID and verified flag gate every claim. Companies sign in the same way.
- **PayPal Payouts to that PayPal ID:** A gift or second-hand owner with no original payment to refund still gets paid, with no onboarding. One key is both PayPal-Request-Id and sender_batch_id, so a retry can never pay twice.
- **Payout webhooks:** Each is signature-verified with PayPal before it updates the console.
- **Fails safe:** If PayPal or the model is down, the claim is held for a person and never lost.

## The evidence room: AG Grid 36 and AG Studio 3

- **Recall to claim link in minutes:** Paste a CPSC recall URL or number; AI drafts the checks from the official record; the company edits and publishes a claim link and QR code.
- **Custom evidence cells:** Photo thumbnails, a decision pill with its reason, an evidence barcode (one bar per check), payout status and a timeline chip. Live every 8 s with cell flash; keyboard-driven.
- **Docked evidence panel:** Every photo, quote and the rule's sentence. Approve takes a second press, re-runs the checks and pays through the same idempotent payout.
- **Insights:** Recall progress against the 6–10% norm, a check funnel and refusal reasons, all cross-filtering. A Recall analyst agent quotes the evidence word for word; by design it has no tool that can approve, reject or pay.
- **CPSC progress report:** A printable draft built from the claim records.

## Where this goes

For recalling companies and recall administrators: stop paying fakes and satisfy the CPSC. Next:

- Each company connects its own PayPal business account: refunds go straight to the owner and Remedy never holds money.
- Transaction Search on the seller's account to tell direct PayPal buyers of a recalled model.
- Every "destroy it and send a photo" recall, then anywhere money should move because a physical act was seen.

Remedy is an independent product built on PayPal's public APIs. It is not made by PayPal.
